subject: Math
subskill: Word Problem - Setup and Solve Inequality
prompt: A bakery makes cakes and pies. Each cake requires $3$ cups of flour and $2$ eggs. Each pie requires $2$ cups of flour and $4$ eggs. The bakery has at most $60$ cups of flour and at most $80$ eggs available. If the bakery must make at least $5$ cakes, what is the maximum number of pies the bakery can make?
explanation: Let $c$ represent the number of cakes and $p$ represent the number of pies. The constraints are: $3c + 2p \leq 60$ (flour), $2c + 4p \leq 80$ (eggs), and $c \geq 5$. To maximize pies, use the minimum number of cakes: $c = 5$. From the flour constraint: $3(5) + 2p \leq 60$, so $2p \leq 45$, giving $p \leq 22.5$. From the egg constraint: $2(5) + 4p \leq 80$, so $4p \leq 70$, giving $p \leq 17.5$. Since $p$ must be a whole number and must satisfy both constraints, the maximum is $p = 17$. Verification: $3(5) + 2(17) = 49 \leq 60$ and $2(5) + 4(17) = 78 \leq 80$.
